case_id.description: The case ID, never the patient's identity.

content_language.description: The language of the documents (BCP 47), for example "cs". Assistant text in the run is in this language.

ExtractionRun.description: One extraction of one case. Never changed after it is written.

id.description: Unique run ID, for example "run-2026-10-19T10:04:11Z-a1b2".

supersedes.description: The run this one replaces; both stay (append-only).

Producer.description: What wrote the run: prepared by hand, the document pipeline, or the NIS (FHIR) import.

engine.description: A deterministic engine and its version, for example "tesseract 5.3.0 ces 4.1.0".

model.description: The model deployment name, from configuration.

prompt.description: The prompt name and version in the repository, for example "extract-facts@3".

RunDocument.description: A document version the run read. The document itself, its parts and its identity check live in D1.

id.description: For example "src-7c1e".

part.description: Stable part ID, or null when the document is not split into parts.

quote.description: Verbatim against the page text named in quote_text, misreadings included ("mg/1", "O").

reported_as.description: "cited" when another document quotes the report (for example "popis z NIS" in an outpatient report).

DocumentSource.description: A passage in a document page.

QuoteText.description: The page text a quote is verbatim against: the PDF's own text layer, Tesseract OCR, or the AI reading.

char_range.description: Start and end offset of the quote in the stored page text.

boxes.description: Word boxes [x, y, width, height] in page pixels.

IdentityResult.description: The identity printed on the page compared with the case's patient. Only the result is stored, never the identity.

ReadingCheck.description: The per-token comparison of the readings that produces the "ověřit" mark.

rule.description: How the readings compare, for example "differ" or "agree".

resource.description: FHIR resource type and ID, for example "Observation/8812".

NisSource.description: A record in the NIS (the hospital system). It is its own evidence: no page, no quote.

id.description: Stable across runs; confirmations, edits and alerts attach to it. For example "f-8d41c2".

key.description: Deterministic from the kind and the identifying values (keys.ts); never a page number or a position.

subject.description: "relative" for family history: a relative's disease never becomes the patient's.

negated.description: The document states the opposite ("bez plicní embolie"). A finding, not a gap.

not_stated.description: Fields of this fact the documents leave open. A field that is simply missing was not looked for.

note.description: The assistant's free-text note about this fact, in the content language.

quarantined.description: Set when a source page shows another patient: kept, but left out of the view, the brief and the rules.

sources.description: Source IDs, all saying the same thing. Empty only for an assistant fact with based_on.

based_on.description: For an assistant fact: the facts it was computed from.

primary.description: The oncological diagnosis the MDT discusses, as opposed to other diagnoses.

DiseaseStatus.description: Disease status as the document says it. Needs review by a clinical expert before real patients.

as_written.description: Verbatim, for example "4/2022", "2.6.2022", "base line CT z 03/2023".

sort.description: ISO form used only for ordering, cut to the precision: "2022-06-02", "2022-04", "2022", or a full timestamp for minute precision.

FactDate.description: A date exactly as the document writes it. A partial date never gets a made-up day.

Origin.description: document: stated in a document; nis: from the NIS; assistant: the assistant's own inference.

text.description: Shown to the doctor in a tooltip, in the content language.

assigned_by.description: "source" when the document or NIS gives the code, "assistant" when we assigned it. A code is never invented.

end_as_written.description: The end of a stay (discharge) as written; null for a visit without one or a stay still going on.

VisitType.description: The kind of visit or stay. "other" when the source names none of these.

length_as_computed.description: The length as computed and shown, for example "38 dní".

IntervalValue.description: Always origin "assistant": a length between two facts, shown as a fact, never a verdict.

id.description: For example "chk-allergy" or "chk-report-mr-brain-2026-09-14".

looks_for.description: A fact kind ("allergy") or a document kind ("original_report").

expected.description: For a document check: the fact whose document is expected.

result.description: found: facts exist; nothing_found: the listed parts say nothing; not_run: this producer does not look.

Check.description: One step of the pipeline that looked for something: what, over which documents, and what came out.

id.description: Derived from rule and subject (keys.ts alertId), so acknowledgements carry over to the next run.

subject.description: What the rule is about: a fact ID, an expected document, a pair of fact IDs ("f-a|f-b", sorted), or a field name.

facts.description: The facts the alert rests on.

note.description: The model's free-text explanation, in the content language.

Alert.description: The result of a rule over facts. The assistant's observation; it never blocks anything.

args.description: Fact IDs or plain values the view formats; never Czech words that would need grammatical case.

AlertMessage.description: A Fluent message (i18n/<locale>/*.ftl) so the alert follows the UI language.

facts.description: The facts the sentence states; a sentence with none is dropped.

QuestionDraft.description: Stays labelled as a draft until a doctor confirms or edits it (D1 question_confirmations).
